correctness.rationale: The icosidodecahedron is the midpoint rectification of the specified icosahedron: the 30 exact Q(sqrt5) midpoint vertices have radius phi, 60 edges of unit length, and degree four. For a central plane avoiding vertices, each section vertex is a transverse edge crossing. At each polyhedron vertex, all four neighbors split into two pairs with each pair sum collinear with the vertex; on the corresponding normal great-circle wall, each pair has opposing projections, so crossing a wall preserves total number of crossed edges. The finite wall arrangement connects all generic directions by paths crossing only one wall at a time; hence # crossing edges is constant. Adjacent radii form angle arccos(phi/2)=pi/5, so Haar edge crossing probability 1/5 and E[N]=60/5=12, fixing every generic N=12. Independently reconstructed all 12 original vertices, 30 distance-2 original edges, 30 rectification vertices, 60 unit edges and all 30 radial pairings exactly in Q(sqrt5); three generic rational normals have exactly 12 crossings. Random diagnostics are unnecessary to infer universal claim.
residual_risks: Planes passing through a vertex are excluded; some nongeneric central equators are decagons.
The key finite pairing lemma checked exactly but the all-directions step requires the wall-crossing topological proof, not sampling.

evidence: General slicing chamber theorem allows counts to change across vertex walls, and generic rectification of other polyhedra need not have 12-sided sections; previously published icosahedron sections have both decagons and dodecagons for a different polytope.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger theorem that all icosidodecahedron central sections have constant count could subsume this, but no such statement verified in inspected primary texts. Face vector alone cannot force directional invariance.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither published icosahedron section counts nor a generic chamber theorem logically entails constant N=12 for the icosidodecahedron. The explicit 30 local vertex identities bridge the gap.

value.rationale: The surprisingly orientation-independent generic section complexity of a non-zonotopal regular Archimedean solid is a complete natural geometric invariant, with an exact probability law and a structural radial-pairing proof. Distinguishes generic 12-gons from special decagon equators and suggests a transferable wall-balance criterion.
residual_risks: The result does not classify perimeter, area, side lengths, or off-center/non-generic sections.

limitations: Only generic central planes avoiding all vertices; nongeneric sections can be 10-sided.
Specialized older literature remains originality risk.
